rationale: Based on title and abstract: clinicopathological findings and treatment in dogs that all had babesiosis plus ehrlichiosis. Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated from the co-infection, and it reads as a routine report of diagnosis and treatment.

title: Efficacy of an imidacloprid/flumethrin collar against fleas, ticks and tick-borne pathogens in dogs.
rationale: Field efficacy trial of an imidacloprid/flumethrin collar against ticks and pathogen transmission; no host pathophysiological data.

title: Babesia canis vogeli, Ehrlichia canis, and Anaplasma platys infection in a dog.
rationale: Based on abstract: a routine single case of a triple infection (diagnosis and treatment). The anaemia, thrombocytopenia and biochemical changes cannot be put down to Babesia, and no distinct syndrome is described.

title: Clinical and hematological study of canine Ehrlichiosis with other hemoprotozoan parasites in Kolkata, West Bengal, India
journal: Asian Pacific journal of tropical biomedicine
rationale: Based on the PMC full text (PMC3793166): haematology is given only pooled for all 47 ehrlichiosis dogs, and only one dog had E. canis plus B. gibsoni. No Babesia-specific host data can be separated.

title: Consensus Recommendations for Treatment for Dogs with Serology Positive Glomerular Disease
rationale: Consensus statement on serology-positive glomerular disease, mainly Borrelia and Leishmania; Babesia is mentioned only in passing with no Babesia-specific data.

title: Prime-boost vaccination with plasmid DNA followed by recombinant vaccinia virus expressing BgGARP induced a partial protective immunity to inhibit Babesia gibsoni proliferation in dogs.
rationale: Based on abstract: a vaccine protection trial whose endpoints are vaccine-antigen antibody titres and parasitaemia after challenge, with no mechanistic host-response outcomes. This follows the round 1-3 precedent for vaccine trials (for example PMID:29279083).

title: Babesiosis in dogs: A report of two different cases
rationale: Based on the abstract, these are two routine diagnosis-and-treatment cases with standard signs and blood counts. The fatal case is put down to hepatic damage and anaemia, but no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation is described, so the case-report exclusion applies.

title: Mycophenolic acid, mycophenolate mofetil, mizoribine, ribavirin, and 7-nitroindole inhibit propagation of Babesia parasites by targeting inosine 5'-monophosphate dehydrogenase.
rationale: IMPDH inhibitors tested on recombinant enzyme, in vitro cultures and a mouse model; drug-target work with no canine host data.

title: Evaluation of doxycycline sensitivity in vitro against Babesia gibsoni by Real Time-PCR
journal: Journal of the Bangladesh Agricultural University
rationale: In vitro doxycycline sensitivity of cultured B. gibsoni by real-time PCR; no host data.

title: Efficacy of Malarone(®) in dogs naturally infected with Babesia gibsoni.
journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
rationale: From the abstract and MeSH: a Malarone/doxycycline trial in 8 dogs with parasitaemia and relapse endpoints. The anaemia and biochemistry are treatment-response measures, not a host-mechanism focus, which matches how rounds 1-3 handled drug trials.

title: The ability of an oral formulation of afoxolaner to block the transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs.
rationale: From the abstract: an acaricide trial on blocking transmission. Hyperthermia in the control dogs served only as an infection endpoint and no host-response data are reported, which matches earlier acaricide-trial exclusions.

title: In vitro and in vivo safety and efficacy studies of amphotericin B on Babesia gibsoni.
rationale: Based on the abstract: a drug efficacy and safety study. The BUN/creatinine rise was AmB nephrotoxicity at 1 mg/kg and the methaemoglobin change was drug-induced in normal erythrocytes in vitro, so neither is host pathophysiology of the infection; the rescue is declined.

title: Trichostatin A, a potential drug for treatment of animal Babesia infections
rationale: In vitro and mouse growth-inhibition study of trichostatin A; no infected-dog host data.

title: Babesia canis infection in a Labrador pup- A clinical case report
rationale: Based on the title only; the OpenAlex record and KrishiKosh landing page give no abstract or journal. The title describes a routine single-pup clinical case report with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.

title: The efficacy of artemisinin, artemether, and lumefantrine against Babesia gibsoni in vitro.
rationale: In vitro drug sensitivity study of artemisinin derivatives; no host data.

title: Clinical use of cardiac troponins in dogs.
rationale: Based on the abstract: a general review of cardiac troponins in dogs. Babesiosis appears only in a list of conditions with raised troponin, so the review's subject is not canine babesiosis; the rescue is declined.

title: Lahore Canine Fever in a Racing Greyhound
journal: Advances in Animal and Veterinary Sciences
rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case of Ehrlichia/Babesia co-infection, diagnosed by smear and cured with imidocarb and doxycycline. The haemorrhagic signs and red urine cannot be attributed to Babesia rather than Ehrlichia, and no mechanistic observation or distinct Babesia syndrome is described.

title: A CASE OF DIPYLIDIASIS AND BABESIOSIS IN A 2-YEAR OLD MONGREL (BITCH) -
rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case with the typical presentation (haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinaemia, leukocytosis) and treatment. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, and its focus is on occurrence and zoonotic advice.

title: Triple Immunosuppressive Therapy of Immune-mediated Hemolytic Anemia in a Dog: Case-report
journal: Bulletin of University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca Veterinary Medicine
rationale: Case report of idiopathic IMHA in a dog that tested negative for Babesia; the dog is not Babesia-infected, so there are no eligible host data.

title: Prevention of transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs treated orally with fluralaner chewable tablets (Bravecto™).
rationale: Based on the abstract: a fluralaner prevention trial whose endpoints are tick efficacy and infection prevention. Rectal temperature and clinical signs were monitored only to detect infection, and infected controls were rescue-treated with no host pathophysiological results reported. This matches earlier rounds, which excluded acaricide prevention trials.

title: Clinical and molecular investigation of a canine distemper outbreak and vector-borne infections in a group of rescue dogs imported from Hungary to Switzerland.
rationale: Canine distemper outbreak report in which a few dogs had vector-borne infections including Babesia; no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.

title: First molecular identification of Babesia gibsoni in dogs from Slovakia, central Europe.
rationale: Two-case report of the first molecular identification of B. gibsoni in Slovakia; the abstract describes diagnosis and treatment with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.

title: Clinical Management of Babesiosis in a Dog along with Blood Transfusion
rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis, doxycycline treatment and transfusion for severe anaemia. The anaemia is the usual presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.

title: Ocorrência de infecção concomitante natural por Ehrlichia sp., Anaplasma sp. E Babesia sp. em cão assistido no hospital veterinário da universidade federal de Uberlândia
journal: Revista Científica Eletrônica de Medicina Veterinária
rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of triple co-infection with diagnosis and treatment. Its cytopenias cannot be attributed to Babesia, so the mixed-infection rule is not met, and it describes no distinct syndrome.

title: Availability of treatments for babesiosis in dogs
rationale: Title concerns the availability of treatments for canine babesiosis, and no abstract is given. The topic is treatment access (likely a letter), not host pathophysiology.

title: Prevention of transmission of Babesia canis by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks to dogs after topical administration of fluralaner spot-on solution.
rationale: Fluralaner prevention of tick transmission of B. canis, with infection status as the endpoint. No host pathophysiological outcomes.

title: New Therapeutic Protocol for Canine Babesiosis: A Case Report
journal: Journal of Dairy Veterinary & Animal Research
rationale: Based on the abstract: a single B. gibsoni case with routine findings (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, fever, splenomegaly) and a report of response to a drug combination. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so the routine case report rule applies.

title: Application of Cryopreserved Packed Red Blood Cells to Treat Anaemic Syndrome in Canine Babesiosis
rationale: Based on the one-page English abstract in the publisher PDF: a treatment study of transfusing cryopreserved packed red cells after Piro-Stop. The only endpoints are percentage rises in Hb, Hct and RBC count against untransfused dogs, with no mechanistic or pathophysiological outcomes.

title: Применение криоконсервированной эритроцитарной массы при коррекции анемического синдрома у собак, вызванного Babesia canis
rationale: Duplicate record of DOI:10.15407/cryo26.02.186 (Russian-language title, same journal page 186). It is a treatment study of red-cell transfusion with only Hb, Hct and RBC response endpoints, so the decision is the same.

title: Clinical management of a Labrador retriever dog concurrently infected with Leptospira interrogans, Babesia gibsoni and Dirofilaria repens
rationale: Title only: no abstract could be found, and the Springer page is behind a sign-in redirect. The title describes clinical management of a single dog with a triple infection including leptospirosis. Findings in such a case cannot be attributed to Babesia, and the title points to a routine management report rather than a distinct syndrome.
